title: fix(pm): `node` is a fireable `Restart-when:` command head
body:
Part of #19129

> **Seat note (skills seat 1, record 5774727539):** this PR delivers the lane grading's direction ① only (the `node` command head, the docblock, the pins). Direction ② — the H9 row naming the channel it read — stays on #19129 as its remainder: the dev measured that `h9OnHoldNoRestartWhen` receives comment bodies as strings and the ids never reach it, so naming the channel is a change to the shared comment cache and ~30 pinned call sites, not a sentence in one function. At MERGED the card returns to the queue with that reading; ⛔ this PR does not close it.

`classifyRestartWhen` in `scripts/pm/check-half-states.mjs` decides whether a `Restart-when:` value is fireable from its FIRST WORD alone, against `RESTART_WHEN_COMMAND_HEADS`. `node` was not on that list, so a runnable `node -e` predicate classified `prose` — the class the H9 row calls "a `manual` in disguise, waiting on an actor nothing schedules" — while the same predicate re-headed `pnpm exec node -e …` classified `command`. `node` is the head every tool in this repo is invoked with, so the row reported a schedulable exit as unschedulable and its remedy sentence pointed at the wrong defect.

## What changed

- `node` joins `RESTART_WHEN_COMMAND_HEADS`, with its corpus provenance in the docblock: the live objectui#9868 hold, whose `Restart-when:` is an installed-surface probe a seat re-headed at 2026-09-18T22:00Z to clear a row this list should never have fired.
- The docblock now states what the head-word test CAN and CANNOT tell. It decides whether some mechanism could run the line at all, which is H9's only question; it cannot tell whether running it means anything, because `node -e "process.exit(0)"` fires on the spot and answers nothing. It records the `pnpm exec` prefix as a workaround for this hole and ⛔ never as a sanctioned spelling.
- The head set stays CLOSED and measured. `node` is in because this repo's own tools are invoked with it and a live hold spells a predicate that way. `bash`, `sh` and `gradle` are NOT added — nobody measured them on a hold — and all three are pinned as `prose` controls so the list cannot drift into a guess at command-shaped words.
- A new floored self-test battery `H9 node command head` (10 cases registered, pin 9) carries the card's four controls plus the closed-list and whole-word controls. `SELF_TEST_BATTERY_FLOOR` rises 8 to 9 and the five sibling pins that assert the roster size move with it, per this file's own floor discipline (a battery deleted from the roster must take its floor with it).

## Evidence

**Red first**, on the dispatch base `7e1b048a1d`, the card's four controls in one command:

```text
HEADS    git|npm|npx|pnpm
SUBJECT  node -e "…" exits 0                        -> prose        (UNFIREABLE)
CONTROL  pnpm exec node -e "…" exits 0              -> command      (FIREABLE)
CONTROL  git grep -q foo -- bar                     -> command      (FIREABLE)
CONTROL  closed objectstack-ai/objectstack#19049    -> closed-ref   (FIREABLE)
CONTROL  someone gets around to it                  -> prose        (UNFIREABLE)
```

**Green**, on this branch — the subject moves and the three controls are byte-identical:

```text
HEADS    git|node|npm|npx|pnpm
SUBJECT  node -e "…" exits 0                        -> command      (FIREABLE)
CONTROL  pnpm exec node -e "…" exits 0              -> command      (FIREABLE)
CONTROL  git grep -q foo -- bar                     -> command      (FIREABLE)
CONTROL  closed objectstack-ai/objectstack#19049    -> closed-ref   (FIREABLE)
CONTROL  someone gets around to it                  -> prose        (UNFIREABLE)
```

**Ablation**, through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` in wrap mode, run from the COMMITTED fix so the restore has a real restore point. Predicted direction: RED.

```text
ablation-replace: anchor   x1 -> x0
ablation-replace: blob     6d9f2f36aef9835f2a47c942528fe74b76c6eb09 -> 4351fce172b838ffc2b4d46eee92f4679ead1b7b
ablation-replace: ok mutation landed: anchor 1 -> 0, blob 6d9f2f36aef9 -> 4351fce172b8
✗ check-half-states self-test: 5 of 5170 case(s) failed.
ablation-replace:   blob after restore  6d9f2f36aef9835f2a47c942528fe74b76c6eb09
ablation-replace:   blob at HEAD        6d9f2f36aef9835f2a47c942528fe74b76c6eb09
ablation-replace:   git diff HEAD       empty
ablation-replace: ok restored: blob == HEAD (6d9f2f36aef9) and `git diff HEAD` is empty
```

The five reds are the two starred subject pins, the two heads-list pins and the gathering-policy pin. Every control in the battery stayed GREEN under the mutation — the `prose` specimens, the closed-list controls and the `pnpm exec` twin — which is what keeps the battery from being a widening nobody can fail. Restore was independently re-read afterwards: worktree blob equals the HEAD blob and `git status --porcelain` is empty.

No `dist/` preflight applies: the subject is a standalone `.mjs` that `node` runs directly, with no build step between the edit and the run.

**Gates**, all on the merged head `d953fabbd`:

- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack --commands` derived 42 families on this tree; all 42 were run and all 42 exited 0. `--ran` reconciles: "42 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 42 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED (a DERIVED zero — all 42 recorded an exit code and none of them is 3)." The family set was re-derived after merging `origin/main` and is identical to the pre-merge one.
- `pnpm check:pm-half-states` exit 0 — 5170 cases pass (5160 at base; the 10 new ones are this battery), batteries line ends `H9 node command head 10/9`.
- `pnpm check:nul-bytes` exit 0, plus a manual control-byte scan of the edited file with zero hits.
- `pnpm lint` (the repo-wide `eslint . --no-inline-config`) exit 0 — the full scan, so no narrowing is being declared.
- Outside the derivation, the roster gates whose roster sits under a directory this path is in were also run: `check-published-list-mirrors` and its self-test, `check-dts-references --self-test`, `check:pm-label-desc-cap`, `check:console-injection`, `check:i18n-stale-fill` — all exit 0. `pnpm check:published-readme-exports` exits **3**, its own PREREQUISITE NOT MET code: this worktree has no `dist/` because this card builds nothing. Recorded as NOT MEASURED — ⛔ not a pass and ⛔ not a finding.

Exit codes throughout were captured into a file and read back before any pipe.

**Changeset:** `skip-changeset`, measured rather than assumed — the root manifest is `private: true`, and of the 75 package manifests in the workspace none carries a `files[]` entry naming `scripts`. `scripts/pm/**` is a repo-root tool directory that ships in nothing.

**Line budget:** +54 / -8, net +46 over one file, against the dispatch's suggested net +30. The overrun is the battery discipline the dispatch itself requires: the roster entry with its rationale, ten pinned cases, and the docblock stating why each candidate head is in or out.

## Acceptance notes

- **The card's second, separable reading is NOT addressed here** — the one asking that the H9 row name the channel it read (the body, or the comment id). The lane's first-touch grading directed it as the same PR on the reasoning that both findings are one function's output; that reasoning does not survive measurement. `h9OnHoldNoRestartWhen` receives `commentBodies` as an array of STRINGS, and the ids never reach it: the shared comment cache that H4, H9 and H17 all ride stores what `commentsFor` returns, which is bodies. Naming an id means changing the shape of that cache and the signature every one of roughly thirty pinned call sites uses — a ripple through three rows, not a sentence in one function. This PR's dispatch scopes the file surface to the command-head defect, and the card itself offers the split ("split it if the lane prefers"). Recommendation: file it as its own card against the same file. Dedupe words: `H9 row channel`, `commentsFor bodies`, `Restart-when comment id`, `h9OnHoldNoRestartWhen signature`.
- No other finding was turned up in this file while working on it.
